title: Resilience Medicine and Metabolic Adaptation in Healthy Aging
content: Physiological resilience refers to the ability of biological systems to maintain function under stress and subsequently restore it. This narrative and integrative review develops a conceptual framework comprising eight functional domains. It links baseline function, functional reserve, stress response, and recovery with the evidence for specific nutraceutical interventions. Mechanistic investigations, observational and intervention studies, as well as evidence syntheses, are categorized according to formulation, dose, population, study duration, comparison group, endpoints, uncertainty, and safety profile. An individual physiological function profile is distinguished from an intervention-related evidence profile. The proposed “multi-system resilience activity” describes in which domains a defined intervention was investigated and what effects were observed. The conditional “resilience breadth” identifies those domains whose findings meet a prede-fined evidence criterion. Representative clinical studies highlight the necessary distinction between physiological changes, functional outcomes, and clinical events. Time-resolved multi-omics analyses, single-cell and spatial metabolomics, Raman imaging, isotope tracing, and population-based models enable complementary investigations of metabolic adaptation processes. The proposed validation separately examines the information gained from additional measurements, the benefits of their temporal recording, the added value of their domain-specific classification, and the outcomes of care tailored to individual functional profiles. The framework proposes empirically testable questions for future evaluation and intervention research; its clinical utility remains to be established.
